newsitem.title: UK: PowerGen in Indonesian, Thai power projects.
newsitem.headline: PowerGen in Indonesian, Thai power projects.

text.p: British electricity generator PowerGen Plc said on Thursday it agreed to take significant stakes in two independent power projects planned in Indonesia and Thailand.
The projects, which will cost 1.27 billion pounds ($2.1 billion), will have a total generating capacity of 1,850 megawatts.
PowerGen said the new projects would boost its international capacity by 34 percent.

"The projects announced today, and a number of other projects which are at the development stage, will reinforce earnings growth from the international business beyond 2001," the company said in a statement.
PowerGen added that within five years, the total output from its international projects would approach the same level as current generation from its UK plants.
The company's shares were marked down 2.0 pence at 691.5 by 0710 GMT.
In Indonesia, PowerGen agreed to take a 40 percent stake in the estimated 398 million pound coal-fired Serang power plant near Cilegon, West Java.
PowerGen said it would project manage the 38-month plant construction programme and would operate the 450MW station when it commissions in early 2001.
Electricity from Serang will be sold to the state electricity company, PLN, under a 30-year contract.
Partners in the project include PT Bukit Sunur Widjaya, with a 40 percent stake, Japan's Sumitomo Corp, with 15 percent, and U.S. group Morrison Knudsen Corp, with five percent.
In Thailand, PowerGen took a 30 percent stake in the 875 million pound Map Ta Phut power station.
PowerGen will operate and maintain the 1,400MW coal-fired station, which will sell electricity to the Electricity Generating Authority of Thailand under a 25-year deal.
Partners in the BLCP Power consortium include Thai companies Banpu and Loxley, both with 30 percent, and global miner Rio Tinto Plc, formerly known as RTZ-CRA.
Rio Tinto took a 10 percent stake and will supply coal for the project.
The Indonesian and Thai developments will be project financed, PowerGen said.
